bullets: Average 0–10 rating and reputation index with change vs the previous period
Negative share, response rate and reply time — by hotel and by manager
Rating and review-count trend over 12 months
Top complaints and praise with quotes, hotels compared by topic
“Other” topics — candidates for the topic dictionary

sections.heading: Brand report
sections.body: The month summary: rating trend, top 5 complaints, changes vs last month and hotels that dropped. It is emailed to brand marketing on the 1st.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Click a complaint topic or the red number in the hotel table to open exactly those reviews in the feed.

hotelReviewsSettings.title: Review settings
hotelReviewsSettings.tagline: Platforms, connections, alerts and AI — no developer needed

sections.heading: Where to start
bullets: Create brands and assign them to hotels
Paste the hotel page links on each platform
Enter the Apify token on the Connections tab
Run “Test” on one hotel and compare the review count with the site
Pick a Telegram bot and alert recipients

sections.heading: About cost
sections.body: Apify charges per collected review and platform prices differ tenfold. Frequency, first load and per-run limit can be set for each platform separately.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If reviews stop arriving, check the Log — it shows errors for every run.

hotelRack.title: Room rack
hotelRack.tagline: Every room by day — who is staying, who is arriving and what is free

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The main working screen for the front desk and reservations: each row is a room, each column a day. A bar is a reservation from arrival to departure, its colour shows the status.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Drag a booking to another room or dates — the system checks the room is free and asks you to confirm
Pull the right edge of a bar to extend or shorten the stay (nightly rate is kept, total is recalculated)
Drag a booking from the “No room” row onto a room to assign it in advance
If the room is occupied, swap the two reservations
Move an in-house guest to another room — a reason is required, the old room becomes “dirty”
Click an empty cell to create a booking with the room and date already filled in
Click a booking to see payment, check-in/check-out and the change history

sections.heading: How to read it
bullets: The room type row shows how many rooms of that type are free each night (red means oversold)
At the bottom: free rooms and occupancy for the whole hotel
Icons on a booking: children, not fully paid, has a note, early check-in / late check-out
Hatching means the room is out of order

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: The rack refreshes itself every 30 seconds — colleagues’ changes appear without reloading.

hotelHousekeeping.title: Housekeeping & rooms
hotelHousekeeping.tagline: Daily cleaning plan, housekeepers, inspection, maintenance, out-of-order rooms and lost & found

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: The cleaning plan builds itself from bookings: departures (full clean), stayovers (service), arrivals (prep) and vacant dirty rooms. Urgent ones go first: same-day turnovers and early arrivals.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Pick housekeepers and press “Assign” — rooms are split by floor, balanced by credits
Assign a housekeeper manually, mark Done, Do not disturb or Inspected (supervisor)
Report an issue with a photo and take the room out of order right away — it returns automatically when the issue is closed
Take a room out of order for a period (repair, renovation) — availability and the room rack account for it
Record a found item with a photo — the owner is matched from the booking in that room, and you can email the guest from the hotel mailbox
Set floor, building and room features

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Housekeepers only need the “Housekeeping” permission — the housekeeper screen works best on a phone.

hotelMyHousekeeping.title: My rooms
hotelMyHousekeeping.tagline: The rooms assigned to you today

sections.heading: How to work
bullets: “Start” when you enter the room, “Done” when it is clean
“Skip” if there is a do-not-disturb sign or the guest declined — enter the reason
“Issue” — describe and photograph what is broken
“Found item” — photograph it and note where you left it

hotelCashier.title: Cashier & services
hotelCashier.tagline: Cashier shift, extra-services catalog and fees

sections.heading: How to work
bullets: Open a shift with the opening cash — every payment until closing goes into it
When closing, count the cash: the system shows what is expected and the difference
A payment from a closed shift cannot be deleted — only refunded
Add services (restaurant, spa, transfer) to charge them to the guest folio in one click
Set % fees for early check-in and late check-out — they are charged automatically

sections.heading: What happens
sections.body: The system checks unarrived guests, guests not checked out, balances and the cash shift, records occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, revenue and payments of the day, moves the business date to the next day and sends a PDF report.

sections.heading: Important
bullets: After closing, money for that day can only be changed with the Night audit permission — corrections are voids in the open day
Auto-audit runs at hotel time and marks no-shows without a penalty

hotelReports.title: PMS reports
hotelReports.tagline: Occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, forecast and pickup

sections.heading: Tabs
bullets: Performance — by day or month and room type, Excel export
Forecast — what is on the books for 30/90/365 days vs the same point last year
Pickup — how many nights were added in the last day, week and month by future date

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The hotel connects to Channex and Channex connects to the OTAs. We send availability per room type and rates per rate plan for each date, and fetch bookings, modifications and cancellations.

sections.heading: What goes to channels
bullets: Availability: free rooms after partner allotments and blocks, out-of-order rooms and held-back rooms — right after any booking
Rate: our rate sheet for the date, by the chosen occupancy and market group, same as a booking
Days without a price or with stop-sale are closed — €0 is never sent

sections.heading: Channel bookings
bullets: Arrive every 5 minutes and show on the rack and in the booking list with the OTA name and booking code
Modifications and cancellations on the OTA update the same booking here
If a room type isn’t mapped the booking isn’t lost: the error is logged and the booking comes again after mapping

sections.heading: How a guest sends a request
bullets: Scans the in-room QR code with the phone camera — no app or sign-up, the page is in their language
Writes to the hotel WhatsApp — if enabled and their phone is on a checked-in booking
Calls the front desk — staff record it with the “Request” button

sections.heading: Where it goes
bullets: Towels, cleaning, amenities, minibar — housekeeping: shown here and on the “My rooms” screen
“Something is broken” — straight to maintenance as an issue, urgent if the guest is in the room
New requests appear for everyone without reloading; you can see how long the guest has been waiting

marketingTraffic.title: Traffic sources and performance
marketingTraffic.subtitle: Data from analytics (GA4, Yandex.Metrica) and ad accounts. Conversions and revenue from analytics; spend and clicks from Ads.

kpi.crHint: Share of sessions that became leads.

guide.openAria: Open step-by-step guide for marketing integrations

marketingIntegrations.title: Marketing integrations
marketingIntegrations.subtitle: Set up analytics and ad accounts (GA4, Metrica, Meta Ads, Google Ads, etc.). Data is used in reports and n8n scenarios.
marketingIntegrations.hint: Sync pulls data into the traffic report (extended metrics by dataSource).
marketingIntegrations.empty: No integrations yet. Add them via API or form (if available).
marketingIntegrations.syncZero: Sync finished, new rows: 0 (empty API response for the period, no counter access, or integration skipped — see backend logs).

form.title: Add integration
form.intro: The new connection will appear in the list on the right. Sync settings are stored in CRM; update via API if needed.
form.currencyLabel: Currency for amounts (cost / revenue in traffic)
form.currencyHint: Sync writes traffic rows in this currency. On the Traffic screen, amounts convert to your report currency using Frankfurter (ECB) rates.
form.name: Name in CRM
form.primaryId: Primary ID (property, counter, ad account, etc.)
form.primaryIdHint: GA4 property ID / Counter ID / Ad Account ID
form.primaryIdHintGa4: GA4 property ID (numeric ID from Admin URL or stream settings)

ga.oauthWizardBanner: The platform Google OAuth client is configured: you can connect GA4 with one Google sign-in using an account that can read this property.

yd.tokenHint: Generate at oauth.yandex.ru for an app with «Yandex.Direct» access (direct:api scope).
yd.clientLoginHint: Only needed when the token was issued to an agency and you want to sync a specific client account.

vk.hint: Get these in the VK Ads cabinet: Settings → API access → "Request API access". The read_ads permission is required. The client secret is shown only once — save it right away.

ads.platformManagedBanner: Google OAuth client and (when set on the server) the Ads developer token are managed by the platform. Enter your Ads customer ID and a refresh token for a Google user who can access that account.
ads.accountModeMccLead: For MCC, enter your manager (MCC) customer ID as Primary ID. Login customer ID is often the same when using that manager account.
ads.managedCustomersEmpty: No eligible client ad accounts found.
ads.managedCustomersCaption: Accounts that will be synced (subject to backend limit)
ads.managedCustomersLoadError: Could not load the list from Google Ads API
ads.managedSyncIncludeHint: Leave blank to sync every account listed above (except exclusions). Separate IDs with comma, space, or newline.
ads.managedSyncExcludeLabel: Do not sync these Customer IDs
ads.managedSyncExcludeHint: Applied after MCC loads the child-account list.

meta.platformAppBanner: The Meta app is configured on the platform; you still need an access token with Ads permissions for your account.
meta.tokenHint: Permanent system-user token from your own Meta app: business.facebook.com/settings → Users → System users → assign the ad account → “Generate token” with the ads_read permission and “Never” expiry. Starts with EAA…. Pick the same currency as the ad account — spend arrives in it.

form.note: “Client secret”, refresh/access tokens, and the Yandex OAuth token are credentials required by Google, Meta, or Yandex—not an arbitrary “CRM secret”. They are stored encrypted. Other fields are IDs, UTMs, etc. You can then use these connections in reports and automations.

table.title: Current integrations
table.syncLookbackHint: UTC calendar days to fetch on sync, inclusive through today. Allowed 30–731; leave empty for default {{defaultDays}}.
table.subtitle: Enabled integrations are used in marketing reports.
table.empty: No integrations yet. Add at least GA4 or Metrica.

callback.connected: Google Analytics 4: access saved; integration list refreshed.
callback.error: Google Analytics 4: sign-in could not be completed. Check redirect URI and analytics.readonly scope in Google Cloud.

oauth.createHint: You will sign in with Google and pick an account that can access this Ads customer. On success the integration is created without pasting a refresh token.

callback.connected: Google Ads: access updated; integration list refreshed.
callback.error: Google Ads: Google sign-in could not be completed. Check the redirect URI in Google Cloud and the adwords OAuth scope.

errors.invalidLookback: Enter a whole number of days from 30 to 731, or leave empty for the default.

metaOauth.connectError: Could not connect the ad accounts
metaOauth.notConfigured: The Meta app is not configured on the platform yet, so Facebook login is unavailable. You can enter an access token manually.
metaOauth.intro: Log in with Facebook and your ad accounts connect without tokens or typing IDs.

Choose the ad accounts you want to see in CRM.
Campaign statistics load right away and update automatically.
metaOauth.permissionsNote: We only request read access to ad data (ads_read): CRM cannot change or launch campaigns.

metaOauth.pickHint: Campaign data loads right after connecting.

metaOauth.doneError: The account is connected, but sync failed: {{error}}

callback.connected: Facebook connected. Choose your ad accounts.
callback.error: Could not log in with Facebook. Please try again.

badge.label: Access

marketingIntegrations.syncBackground: A large account is still syncing in the background — data will appear in 1–2 minutes.

marketingAutomations.title: Marketing automations (n8n)
marketingAutomations.subtitle: Track n8n scenarios: traffic import, campaigns, audience sync. Later you can pull status from the n8n API.

form.title: New scenario
form.name: Scenario name
form.note: You can add tokens, schedule, and run status for each scenario.

list.title: Current automations

marketingSeo.title: SEO
marketingSeo.subtitle: Your site’s organic traffic and load speed — from Google Search Console and PageSpeed Insights, refreshed on demand.

errors.gscNotSynced: GSC not synced: check property access.
errors.psiNotSynced: PageSpeed not synced: check key and URL.
errors.gscForbidden: The connected Google account has no access to {{property}}. Make sure you connected the Google account in which the site is added to Search Console, or pick a site from the available ones.
errors.psiReconnect: To enable speed measurements, reconnect your Google account — one extra permission is needed. Or add your own PageSpeed API key.
errors.psiApiDisabled: Google rejected the speed measurement: PageSpeed Insights API is not enabled in the platform’s Google Cloud project. The project owner needs to enable it once (it takes a few minutes to apply), then press “Refresh”. Or add your own PageSpeed API key.

connections.title: Site SEO check

steps.t: compare with the previous period; falling impressions with a steady CTR usually mean lost rankings, not lost demand.
below 2% at a top-10 position points to a weak page title and description.
keep the number trending down; a sharp rise means new low-volume queries got indexed.
LCP under 2.5 s and CLS under 0.1 on mobile; re-check after every site release.

keyHelp.title: How to get a PageSpeed API key
keyHelp.intro: The key is free and takes a couple of minutes to create in Google Cloud Console — any Google account will do.

steps.t: open Google Cloud Console and create a project (or pick an existing one).
find “PageSpeed Insights API” in the API library and click “Enable”.
recommended: in the key settings → “API restrictions” → select only “PageSpeed Insights API”.
copy the key (starts with AIzaSy…), paste it into “PageSpeed API key”, press “Save”, then “Refresh”.

keyHelp.note: A free key allows 25,000 measurements a day. The key is stored in CRM and only ever shown masked in the interface.

integrations.connectWhatsappIntro: Connect a WhatsApp Business number through Meta's official WhatsApp Cloud API: client messages arrive in the CRM, you can reply from the lead card, and AI employees can hold the conversation. Below is a step-by-step guide on where to find each value.
integrations.connectWhatsappTokenHint: Permanent system-user token starting with EAA… (step 4). The temporary token from the “Try it” page won't do — it stops working within a day.
integrations.connectWhatsappWabaIdHint: Next to the Phone number ID: “WhatsApp” use case → “Step 1. Try it”. The CRM uses it to subscribe the app to incoming messages automatically.

waGuide.title: 📘 Step-by-step guide: where to find the data (30–40 minutes)
waGuide.intro: You need a Facebook account and a phone number for WhatsApp. The number must not be in use in the WhatsApp app on a phone: use a separate number (a landline works too) or delete the WhatsApp account on it in the app. Company documents are not needed to receive messages and reply to clients.
waGuide.fieldsTitle: What to enter in the form

fields.phoneNumberId: Phone number ID — required (step 3). Not the phone number itself but a long numeric ID
fields.wabaId: WhatsApp Business Account ID — recommended (step 3): the CRM subscribes the app to messages itself
fields.verifyToken: Verify token — required: make up any Latin string without spaces, e.g. company-wa-2026, and write it down
fields.appSecret: App Secret — required (step 5): without it incoming messages are rejected
fields.label: Name in CRM — optional
fields.notNeeded: Webhook URL and Email are not needed for WhatsApp

waGuide.step1Body: Open business.facebook.com and log in with Facebook. If your company has no portfolio yet, create one: company name, your name, work email.
waGuide.step2Body: developers.facebook.com → “My Apps” → “Create app” → use case “Connect with customers through WhatsApp” → pick your business portfolio → “Create”. Meta creates a WhatsApp Business Account and gives you a test number.
waGuide.step3Title: Phone number ID and WhatsApp Business Account ID
waGuide.step3Body:
In the app: “Use cases” → “Connect on WhatsApp” → “Step 1. Try it”. Under the number you'll see “Phone Number ID” and “WhatsApp Business Account ID” — copy both.
Your own number instead of the test one: “Add phone number” on the same page → display name (your company name as on the website), category → number → code from SMS or call. Then “Step 2. Set up your workspace” → “Register your WhatsApp phone number” → set a 6-digit PIN and keep it. Enter the ID of your own number in the form.
waGuide.step4Body:
business.facebook.com/settings → “Users” → “System users” → “Add”: any name, role “Admin”.
Open the user → “Assign assets”: “Apps” → your app → “Full control”. “Assign assets” again: “WhatsApp accounts” → your account → “Full control”.
Click “Generate token”: app — yours, expiry — “Never”, permissions — whatsapp_business_messaging and whatsapp_business_management. Copy the string starting with EAA: Meta won't show it again.
waGuide.step5Body:
developers.facebook.com → your app → “App settings” → “Basic” → “App secret” → “Show” (Facebook asks for your password) — that's the App Secret.
On the same page fill in “Privacy Policy URL” (the policy page on your website) and “Category”, then “Save changes” — the app can't be published without them.
waGuide.step6Title: Save the connection in the CRM
waGuide.step6Body: Fill in this form and click “Save and test”. The CRM checks the token and number with Meta and subscribes the app to messages. The connection card will show the webhook address (Callback URL) — you need it in the next step.
waGuide.step7Body:
In the app: “Connect on WhatsApp” → “Step 2. Set up your workspace” → “Configure webhooks”.
“Callback URL” — the address from the connection card in the CRM. “Verify token” — the same Verify token as in the form, character for character.
“Verify and save” → in the webhook fields list, subscribe to messages.
waGuide.step8Body:
On the left, “Publish” → “Publish”: until the app is published, real client messages are not delivered.
Write to the number from your phone — the message appears in the WhatsApp section and on the lead card (a new lead is created if the number isn't in the CRM yet). The Meta test number can only chat with numbers on its recipient list (up to 5).
waGuide.pricing: 💬 Pricing: client messages and your replies within 24 hours of their last message are free. Writing to a client first is only possible with Meta templates and needs a payment method in WhatsApp Manager. Business verification with documents is only needed if you message more than 250 new clients first per day.

mailchimpCampaignAction.replyToHint: Must be an address on a domain verified in Mailchimp (Website / Domains), otherwise the API returns an error.
mailchimpCampaignAction.campaignTitleHint: Visible only in Mailchimp; defaults to subject. Max 100 characters.
mailchimpCampaignAction.htmlBodyHint: Full email for the entire audience. You can copy from Emails / marketing templates.
mailchimpCampaignAction.textBodyHint: Plain text for clients without HTML; reduces spam likelihood.

zapierAction.intro: Send JSON to Zapier Catch Hook (or a Make equivalent via webhook).

googleAdsAction.intro: Arbitrary Google Ads API request: method, path, and JSON body (GAQL, etc.). For integrations and non-standard flows. Typical “CRM report” users do not need this step — see the block below.
googleAdsAction.forClientBody: This is not a report wizard: here you configure a direct ads API call. For a ready-made CRM report (sales, leads, tasks…) to email or Telegram without paths and JSON — use “Send report”.
googleAdsAction.marketingIntegrationHint: The CRM exchanges refresh token for access token when the step runs (as for report sync). Override fields below take priority if filled.
googleAdsAction.noMarketingIntegrations: No active Google Ads integration in Marketing.
googleAdsAction.usingMarketingCredentials: A marketing integration is selected — developer token, OAuth, and Customer ID are pulled when the step runs. You do not need to re-enter them here; fields below are overrides only.
googleAdsAction.crmConnectionOptionalAbsent: There is no separate Google Ads connection under Automations → Integrations — not required for this step if a marketing integration is selected above.
googleAdsAction.noConnections: No Google Ads connection under Automations → Integrations. Needed only if you do not use the marketing integration above.
googleAdsAction.developerTokenHint: If a connection with developer token is selected, you can leave the field empty.
googleAdsAction.customerIdHint: Inserted into the path as {{customerId}}. If Customer ID is set in “Webhook URL” on the connection, it is picked up automatically.
googleAdsAction.paramsJsonHint: For POST/PATCH/PUT — Google Ads API body. Placeholders {{lead.name}}, etc. Not sent for GET.

metaAdsAction.intro: Arbitrary Meta Marketing API (Graph) request: path, method, body if needed. For integrations. For a typical scheduled CRM report use “Send report” — see the block below.
metaAdsAction.forClientBody: This step is for direct Graph API calls. A ready CRM report to email or Telegram is configured with “Send report” (report type, channel, schedule).
metaAdsAction.marketingIntegrationHint: Access token is taken from the marketing integration settings. The override field below takes priority.
metaAdsAction.noMarketingIntegrations: No active Meta Ads integration in Marketing.
metaAdsAction.usingMarketingCredentials: A marketing integration is selected — the access token comes from there. No need to duplicate; use override below only if needed.
metaAdsAction.crmConnectionOptionalAbsent: There is no separate Meta connection under Automations → Integrations — optional when a marketing integration is selected.
metaAdsAction.noConnections: No Meta Ads connection under Automations → Integrations. Needed only if you do not use the marketing integration above.
metaAdsAction.paramsJsonHint: For POST/PATCH/PUT — JSON body. Not used for GET. Placeholders {{lead.name}}, etc.

whatsappAction.intro: WhatsApp Cloud API: text message type. The connection must include Phone number ID and token from Meta.

whatsappAction.toHint: If empty, the lead/contact phone from the trigger is used. Digits with country code.

conn.googleAccessNote: Google grants Business Profile API access on application; without approval the quota is zero. You need a Google Cloud project, OAuth with the business.manage scope and the account that owns the hotel profiles. Until access is granted, Google can be read temporarily via Apify (Google Maps link on the hotel).
conn.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect Google Business Profile? Replies from CRM to Google will stop.
conn.accountsError: Couldn't load accounts — check that API access has been approved
conn.step1: Create a Pub/Sub topic in the same Google Cloud project.
conn.step2: Grant the Pub/Sub Publisher role to Google's service account:
conn.step3: Create a push subscription to this address:
conn.step4: Save the topic and enable notifications — new reviews will arrive instantly.
conn.googleNightly: Safety net: every night CRM re-checks the last 30 days and the totalReviewCount; a mismatch over the threshold alerts the developer.
conn.apifyText: Booking.com, Tripadvisor, Yandex, Expedia, Check24, Otelpuan (and HolidayCheck for reading) are collected by ready-made Apify scrapers on a schedule. You pay per result, so after the first load only fresh reviews are fetched.
conn.tokenRemoveConfirm: Remove the Apify token? Platform collection will stop.
conn.offSeasonHint: Apify platforms are collected once a day — saves budget
conn.actorsHint: Each platform has its own scraper, frequency and limits: Apify charges per review returned and prices differ tenfold (Google ~$0.5 per 1000, Otelpuan ~$29). Scheduled runs fetch only new reviews. After two consecutive failures CRM switches to the fallback actor. Input is a JSON template: {{u}}, {{m}}, {{s}} are filled in at run time.
conn.googleFallbackActor: temporary read-only Google collection until the API is approved
conn.hcReadActor: reads reviews; replies go via the API below
conn.hcNote: The key is generated per hotel in HolidayCheck Business Center and entered on the Hotels & platforms tab. There's no public API documentation — request it from HolidayCheck and enter the reply endpoint and format here.
conn.maxConcurrentHint: Apify Free plan — up to 5, Starter — up to 32.
conn.usageOver: Collection is paused: raise the limit in Apify → Billing; collection resumes on its own within 15 minutes.

live.offTitle: No live connection — refreshing every 30 seconds, reconnecting

channels.title: Sales channels
channels.subtitle: Booking.com, Expedia, Airbnb and other OTAs via Channex: rates and availability go out automatically, bookings land on the room rack.
channels.connectHint: Channex is a channel manager: one key gives access to Booking.com, Expedia, Airbnb and 50+ other OTAs. OTAs are connected in the Channex account — only the key goes here.
channels.step1: Register the property in Channex (app.channex.io) and connect the OTAs you need there.
channels.step2: Create an API key in your Channex profile (API Keys) and paste it below.
channels.step3: Map room types and rate plans — rates and availability start flowing out, bookings start landing on the rack.
channels.noPropertyHint: The account has several properties — choose which one is this hotel:
channels.pulled: Channel bookings: new {{created}}, modified {{modified}}, cancelled {{cancelled}}, errors {{failed}}
channels.autoOn: availability instantly, bookings every 5 min, rates every 30 min
channels.mappingHint: One channel room per our room type; a room can have several rate plans (BAR, with breakfast…). Availability goes per room, prices and restrictions per rate plan: the season price list by occupancy and market group, stops and restrictions from the calendar. Days without a price are not sold.
channels.currencyWarn: The Channex rate plan currency differs from the hotel currency ({{currency}}) — rates are sent in the hotel currency without conversion.
channels.pushDaysHint: How many days ahead to open sales on channels (7–500; Channex certifies a full sync of 500 days).
channels.reserveHint: This many rooms of each type are not given to channels — for direct sales and partners.
channels.disconnectBody: Sync with Channex stops and mappings are deleted. Bookings already received from channels stay.
channels.fullBody: Send prices, availability and restrictions for the whole window again? Channex allows a full sync once a day — it normally runs by itself at night.
channels.syncNothing: Everything is already in the channel — no changes
channels.syncDone: Sent: availability {{availability}}, prices and restrictions {{rates}} ({{calls}} calls)
channels.syncDeferred: part was deferred by the channel limit — it goes out within a minute
channels.syncWarnings: the channel rejected {{count}} values — see the log
channels.fullRule: once a day, at night hotel time
channels.accepted: accepted by the channel: availability {{avail}}, rates {{rates}}
channels.pausedUntil: Sync is paused after a channel error until {{at}} — it then resumes by itself. “Resume” lifts the pause now.
channels.webhookOnHint: Webhook is on: the channel reports a new booking at once and it loads within seconds.
channels.webhookOffHint: Webhook is off: bookings are polled every 5 minutes.
channels.availabilityOnly: No rate plan — only availability is sent. Add a rate plan to send prices and restrictions.
channels.derivedNote: Derived rate plan: the channel calculates the price, only restrictions are sent
channels.perPersonNote: Per-person price: sent for each number of guests

hint.per_room: Per-room price — by the chosen occupancy

promos.deleteBody: Delete the promotion? Existing bookings keep their discount — it is stored in the booking.
promos.emptyText: Add an early booking offer (−30% when booked by 31 Jan with 50% prepayment) or import the EARLY BOOKING block together with the season price list.

typeHint.last_minute: Discount for bookings shortly before arrival — to sell remaining rooms.
typeHint.spo: Special offer for stay dates: e.g. −15% in May.
typeHint.long_stay: Discount for longer stays: % from N nights or “7 nights — 1 free”.

ruleHint.nights: Only nights inside the period are discounted: a stay 8–12 Nov with the period ending 10 Nov gets 2 discounted nights.

bookHint.last_minute: E.g. 7 — discount for bookings made no earlier than 7 days before arrival.

promos.combineHint: Combinable promotions add up (max 90% per night). Of the non-combinable ones, one applies — the best for the guest by discount amount.
promos.prepayHint: The booking’s prepayment deadline is the earliest of the rate plan and the promotion. If not paid on time, the booking card offers “Remove promotion discount”.

guests.title: Guests
guests.subtitle: One guest card across all hotels: stays, revenue, preferences, VIP and blacklist. Profiles are built from bookings automatically — by email, phone and passport.

welcome.body: This will take less than a minute. We'll help you invite your team and show you what the CRM looks like with real data — before you start adding your own.

team.title: Invite your team
team.body: Add colleagues who will work with leads, sales, or bookings. You can also do this later, at any time, in the "Staff" section.

sample.title: Fill with sample data?
sample.body: We'll add a couple of leads, a contact, a company, products, and two projects with tasks — all marked "[Sample]" so you can immediately see how the CRM works: the pipeline, cards, projects, analytics. All of it can be removed with one click at any time from settings.

done.title: All set up
done.body: You're ready to go. This guide won't show again — you can't come back to it, but everything you did here (invitations, sample data) will remain available in the regular CRM sections.

ai.title: Tell us about your business
ai.body: A couple of sentences: what you do, where, what you sell and where clients come from. AI will suggest a CRM setup — you choose what to apply.
ai.placeholder: E.g.: a 40-room boutique hotel in Antalya, guests book via Booking and message us on WhatsApp, we also sell transfers and tours.

err.AI_UNAVAILABLE: AI is temporarily unavailable — skip this step, you can set things up later.

items.a: Lumiva CRM is a cloud platform for managing clients, projects, and sales. It includes a CRM, no-code workspaces, automations, analytics, and integrations with popular services.

items.q: What kind of business is Lumiva for?
items.a: Small and medium businesses: from freelancers and startups to teams of 50–200 people. Used in sales, marketing, project management, and client service.

items.q: Do I need to install anything on my computer?
items.a: No. Lumiva CRM runs in the browser — on desktop and on your phone. No installation or server maintenance is required.
Yes. After sign-up you get 14 days of the Enterprise plan with full access, no card required. Then pick a plan — your data is kept.
Monthly or yearly. Yearly billing gives a 10% to 20% discount depending on the plan. Payment by bank card: iyzico and PayTR in Turkey, YooKassa in Russia, Stripe elsewhere.
Yes, at any time. If the plan is not renewed, access to the CRM is paused and your data is not deleted.

items.q: Are there discounts for nonprofits and schools?
items.a: Yes. Email us at hello@lumiva.agency with supporting documents and we'll work out individual terms.
Each company's data is isolated at the database level. Connections go over HTTPS only, passwords are stored as hashes, and two-factor sign-in is available. The database is backed up every night.

items.q: Is there an API for integrations?
items.a: Yes. A REST API with token authentication: lead intake, products, bookings and other objects. See the API section for docs.

items.q: Can I import data from another CRM?
items.a: Yes. Leads, products and workspace tables can be imported from Excel/CSV. amoCRM, Bitrix24 and HubSpot have ready-made integrations.

items.q: How do you monitor the platform?
items.a: Website and API availability is checked automatically every 5 minutes, and the team is alerted immediately about failures. We announce planned maintenance in advance.

WhatsApp, Telegram, email, SMS, Google Ads, Meta Ads, Yandex Direct, VK Ads, Google Analytics 4, Yandex Metrika, WooCommerce, Shopify, WordPress CF7, amoCRM, Bitrix24, HubSpot, Mailchimp, Slack, MS Teams, Google Sheets, Google Calendar, Outlook, Jira, 1C, SAP, Zapier, Make, iyzico, PayTR, YooKassa, OpenAI and Anthropic.

items.q: How do I connect a Telegram bot?
items.a: In the "Telegram" section, create a bot and paste the token from @BotFather. Once connected, all client messages land in the CRM and you can reply right from the interface.
Yes. Incoming webhooks accept leads from websites, forms and bots, and automations can send outgoing webhooks to your URL.

sections.title: 1. General provisions
sections.content:
This Privacy Policy (the "Policy") describes how Lumiva CRM (the "Company", "we", "us") collects, uses, stores, and protects the personal data of users of the lumiva.agency platform (the "Platform", "Service").

By using the Platform, you agree to the terms of this Policy. If you do not agree, please stop using the Service.

The Policy applies to all users: individuals, organization representatives, and any other people interacting with the Platform. It covers all products, websites, and mobile apps operating under the Lumiva CRM brand.

sections.title: 2. What data we collect
sections.content:
**2.1 Data you provide directly:**
- First name, last name, or a display name
- Email address
- Phone number (when filling out forms)
- Organization name and job title
- Payment details (processed by the payment provider, not stored on our servers)
- Any data entered into the CRM (contacts, deals, notes, files)

**2.2 Data collected automatically:**
- IP address and country/city-level geolocation
- Browser type, operating system, screen resolution
- Login date and time, session duration
- Pages and features you visit and use
- UTM tags and referral sources
- Error and crash data (logs)

**2.3 Data from third-party sources:**
- Information from connected integrations (Google Analytics, Meta Ads, AmoCRM, and others) — only to the extent you explicitly authorized when connecting
- Publicly available profile data (if you sign in via OAuth)

sections.title: 3. Purposes of processing
sections.content:
We process your data solely for the following purposes:

**3.1 Providing the Service:**
Creating and managing your account, granting access to CRM features, syncing data across devices, fulfilling contractual obligations.

**3.2 Improving the product:**
Analyzing feature usage, identifying bugs and bottlenecks, prioritizing new development. Data is anonymized or aggregated before analysis.

**3.3 Communication:**
Sending transactional emails (registration confirmation, password reset, plan change notices) and responding to support requests. Marketing emails only with your explicit consent.

**3.4 Security:**
Preventing fraud, unauthorized access, and abuse. Complying with legal requirements.

**3.5 Billing:**
Issuing invoices, processing payments, keeping financial records. Transaction data is retained in accordance with tax law requirements.

sections.title: 4. Legal basis
sections.content:
We process data on the following legal bases:

**Contract performance** — when processing is necessary to provide the Service you requested (account creation, transactions).

**Legitimate interest** — for improving security, preventing abuse, and enhancing the product. In these cases we balance our interests against your privacy rights.

**Consent** — for marketing emails and analytics cookies. You may withdraw consent at any time without affecting your use of the Service.

**Legal obligation** — when processing is required to comply with applicable law (tax, accounting, or regulator requests).

sections.title: 5. Storage and protection of data
sections.content:
**5.1 Where data is stored:**
Data is stored on servers in a data center in the European Union (Lithuania). A database backup is created daily.

**5.2 Retention periods:**
- Account and CRM data: for the full term of the contract + 30 days after account deletion
- Financial documents: 5 years (legal requirement)
- Technical logs: 90 days
- Support request data: 2 years

**5.3 Protection measures:**
- Encryption in transit: HTTPS (TLS)
- Passwords stored only as hashes
- Two-factor authentication for users
- User action log
- Multi-tenant architecture: each account is isolated at the database level
- Restricted staff access to data — only on a documented need basis and on request

**5.4 Incident notification:**
In the event of a data breach that could pose a risk to your rights, we will notify you and the relevant regulators within the timeframes required by law (no later than 72 hours).

sections.title: 6. Sharing data with third parties
sections.content:
We **do not sell** your personal data to third parties.

**6.1 Contractors and sub-processors:**
We may share data with trusted service providers who help us operate: cloud infrastructure, payment systems, support services. Every sub-processor is bound by a contract requiring data protection standards no less strict than ours.

**6.2 Integrations you choose:**
If you connect third-party services (Google, Meta, Telegram, etc.), data is shared with those services per their own privacy policies. You can disconnect an integration at any time.

**6.3 Corporate transactions:**
In the event of a merger, acquisition, or sale of assets, your data may be transferred to the new owner — with notice to you and your rights preserved.

**6.4 Legal requirements:**
We may disclose data in response to a valid request from government authorities, courts, or regulators. In such cases, we aim to notify you unless prohibited by law.

sections.title: 7. Your rights
sections.content:
You have the following rights regarding your personal data:

**Right of access** — request confirmation of whether we process your data, and obtain a copy of it.

**Right to rectification** — request correction of inaccurate or incomplete data. Most data can be updated yourself in account settings.

**Right to erasure ("right to be forgotten")** — request deletion of your personal data. We will delete data no longer needed for the processing purposes, except where retention is legally required.

**Right to restrict processing** — request that processing be paused in certain situations (for example, while you dispute its accuracy).

**Right to data portability** — receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format (CSV/JSON) to transfer to another provider.

**Right to object** — object to processing based on legitimate interest, including for direct marketing.

**Right to withdraw consent** — withdraw previously given consent at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of processing before withdrawal.

To exercise any of these rights, contact **privacy@lumiva.agency**. We will respond within 30 days. If we decline a request, we will explain why.

sections.title: 8. Cookies
sections.content:
**8.1 What cookies are:**
Cookies are small text files stored by your browser. We use them to run the Service, for analytics, and for personalization.

**8.2 Types of cookies:**

*Essential (technical)* — required for the Platform to work: authentication, security, load balancing. Cannot be disabled.

*Analytics* — help us understand how the Service is used (Google Analytics 4, Yandex Metrica). Data is anonymized. Can be disabled in settings.

*Marketing* — used to show relevant ads (Meta Pixel, Google Ads). Set only with your consent.

**8.3 Managing cookies:**
You can manage cookies via your browser settings or the consent banner on first visit. Disabling analytics cookies does not affect CRM functionality.

sections.title: 9. Cross-border data transfers
sections.content:
If you are located in the EU/EEA, the UK, or another jurisdiction with cross-border transfer restrictions, we apply appropriate safeguards:

- Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) approved by the European Commission
- Transfers to countries with an adequacy decision
- Specific legal mechanisms for particular jurisdictions

A list of countries and mechanisms used is available on request at privacy@lumiva.agency.

sections.title: 10. Data Processing Agreement (DPA)
sections.content:
If your organization uses Lumiva CRM to process your customers' personal data, you are the controller and we are the data processor.

We're ready to sign a Data Processing Agreement, which includes:
- A description of data subject categories and data types
- Processing purposes and instructions
- Technical and organizational security measures
- Terms for engaging sub-processors
- Incident response procedures

To request a DPA template or negotiate individual terms, contact privacy@lumiva.agency.

sections.title: 11. Children and minors
sections.content:
Lumiva CRM is intended for use by people 18 years of age or older (or the age of digital consent in your jurisdiction).

We do not knowingly collect children's data. If we learn that a child's data was collected without parental consent, we will delete it immediately.

If you believe a child has provided us with data, please contact us at privacy@lumiva.agency.

sections.title: 12. Changes to this Policy
sections.content:
We may update this Policy from time to time. For material changes, we will notify you by email or via a banner on the Platform at least 14 days before the change takes effect.

The date of the last update is shown at the bottom of the page. Continued use of the Service after changes take effect constitutes acceptance of the revised Policy.

Previous versions of the Policy are available on request.

sections.title: 13. Use of Google API Services data
sections.content:
If you connect your Google account to Lumiva CRM, we request access only to the services you explicitly select when connecting:

**Gmail** — reading and sending email on behalf of the connected mailbox, so that conversations appear inside the CRM and you can send messages to customers directly from the system. We do not use email content to serve ads, do not share it with third parties, and do not use it to train general-purpose AI models.

**Google Calendar** — reading and creating events in your connected calendar to keep meetings in sync with the CRM.

**Google Sheets** — exporting and importing CRM data to and from the spreadsheets you connect.

**Google Ads** — read-only access to spend and campaign statistics of the ad account you connect, shown in the "Marketing" section.

**Google Analytics** — read-only access to website traffic data from the GA4 property you connect.

**Google Search Console** — read-only access to organic search data for the site you connect.

**Retention and deletion:** data obtained through these services is retained only for as long as the connection is active and is deleted within 30 days of disconnecting it. Access tokens are stored encrypted and used solely to make API requests on your behalf.

**Revoking access:** you can disconnect any of these integrations at any time in the "Integrations" section of Lumiva CRM, or directly in your Google Account settings at myaccount.google.com/permissions.

**Limited Use:** Lumiva CRM's use and transfer to any other app of information received from Google APIs will adhere to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.

sections.title: 14. Contact us
sections.content:
For privacy questions, exercising your rights, or inquiries related to data processing:

**Email:** privacy@lumiva.agency
**General questions:** hello@lumiva.agency
**Contact form:** lumiva.agency/contact

A Data Protection Officer (DPO) has been appointed and is reachable at the contacts above.

If you believe your rights have been violated, you also have the right to lodge a complaint with the supervisory authority in your country (in Russia — Roskomnadzor, in the EU — your member state's supervisory authority).

security.title: Security & Data Protection
security.subtitle: How data protection actually works in Lumiva CRM — infrastructure, application, and access. No marketing promises, only what's actually implemented.

s1Items.title: Encryption in transit
s1Items.desc: All connections to the platform go over HTTPS (TLS) only.

s1Items.title: Two-factor authentication
s1Items.desc: Sign-in can be protected with a code from an authenticator app; backup codes are available.

s1Items.title: Password storage
s1Items.desc: User passwords are stored as bcrypt hashes — the password itself is never stored in plain text or recoverable, only resettable.

s2Items.title: Multi-tenant architecture
s2Items.desc: Each customer's (tenant's) data is isolated at the database level — one tenant cannot reach another's data through the API.

s2Items.title: Role-based access control (RBAC)
s2Items.desc: Access to sections and actions is determined by staff role within the tenant; newer modules have granular permissions (e.g. separate rights for pricing, settings, catalog management).

s3Items.title: Rate limiting
s3Items.desc: The API is protected against overload and brute-force attempts: 20 requests per second and 100 requests per 10 seconds.

s3Items.title: Security HTTP headers
s3Items.desc: Applied via Helmet — protection against clickjacking, MIME-sniffing, and other common header-level attacks.

s3Items.title: Short-lived access tokens
s3Items.desc: Sessions run on signed tokens with a limited lifetime; the signing secret is mandatory and has no default value.

s3Items.title: Configurable CORS
s3Items.desc: The list of allowed origins is set explicitly via an environment variable, not left open to any source.

security.s4Text: The action log records who changed what in the CRM, with date and time. For products we also keep a detailed history of price, cost, status, SKU and barcode.
security.s5Title: Privacy and control over your data

s5Items.title: Export and deletion on request
s5Items.desc: You can request an export or deletion of your data — timelines and process are described in the Privacy Policy.

s5Items.title: Where data is stored
s5Items.desc: Servers are located in the European Union (Lithuania). The database is backed up every night.

security.s5PrivacyLink: More details in the Privacy Policy
security.s6Text: If you've found a security issue, contact us directly — we prioritize responding to these reports.

prog.debtsHint: Built-in program. Unpaid sales — a polite email to the client with a payment link (iyzico / PayTR / YooKassa). Every email after your approval.
prog.finWeekHint: Built-in program. Week over week: paid, awaiting payment, refunds, who owes — the system computes the numbers, the department writes conclusions.
prog.watchHint: Built-in program. Every morning: campaigns spending for {{days}} days without conversions — an instant notification to you and a review by the department with a pause/cut proposal. Awareness campaigns are left alone.
prog.budgetHint: Built-in program. ROAS and cost per conversion by campaign over 14 days → a proposal: what to cut, what to scale. Every change in the ad account only after your approval.
prog.followupHint: Built-in program. If the client is silent after our message — short useful follow-ups on these days, stops on reply. After {{lose}} silent days — status lost.
prog.reactHint: Built-in program. Weekly, up to {{n}} leads lost more than {{days}} days ago get one warm message. Not again within six months.
prog.stockHint: Built-in program. Every morning the system checks stock and 30-day usage; items that are out, below threshold or will run out within 14 days become one task: group by supplier and prepare orders. Every purchase order goes out after your approval.
prog.prHint: Built-in program. Every hour the department checks the repository: a new PR or new commits in it → it reads the diff and CI status and posts a review with line comments. It never approves or merges — that is your call.
prog.slaHint: Built-in program. Every hour: tickets where the client has waited longer than {{h}} h become a task for the department right away. Works even if a scenario was off or a reply was rejected.
prog.remindHint: Built-in program. Guests whose visit or check-in is tomorrow get an email with date, time, address and directions (from the Brain). During the department’s daytime.
prog.confirmHint: Built-in program. A booking has waited more than 2 hours — the department confirms it by the Brain rules or reports what blocks it.
prog.noshowHint: Built-in program. The booking time passed and the guest is not checked in — the department marks a no-show and politely offers a new time.
prog.reviewHint: Built-in program. After the visit or check-out — a thank-you and the review link from the Brain. Without a link nothing is sent.
prog.reconcileHint: Built-in program. Every day: paid but the sale is not marked; payment amount differs; the client could not pay — the department handles each row. Marking as paid goes after your approval.
